proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Grim Ward caused monsters to FLEE, making it actively harmful to melee builds. Corpse requirement (consume a corpse to place) wasted the resource barbarians needed for Find Item. It also did not stack with other fear/warcry effects and blocked other corpse interactions. The feared-enemy anti-synergy with melee is the intrinsic design flaw — no external tuning could fix it while the skill feared enemies. Patch 2.4 finally gave it physical resistance reduction to enemies, partially mitigating the flight-and-chase problem; Patch 2.5 further buffed it to real utility. Dead for ~20 years because of the run-away-from-melee-attacker design failure.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Impale's intrinsic design flaw: huge single-hit damage but applied a WEAPON DURABILITY COST per use, the chance only decreasing with skill investment, and the attack was extremely slow (reduced attack speed). Single-target only with brutal recovery time. The durability drain on expensive runeword weapons was existentially punishing — the attack literally destroyed your gear faster than you could farm. No external tuning could remove this self-destructive property while the mechanic existed. Patch 2.4 made it uninterruptible and applied a slow, partially rehabilitating it for PvE spear builds, but for 20 years the durability cost + glacial IAS was the intrinsic kill.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Sacrifice's self-damage scales multiplicatively with weapon damage output: 8% of damage dealt returned to the caster. This means more powerful weapons make the skill MORE dangerous to use. Life leech requirements scale with difficulty (16% Nightmare, 24% Hell) just to break even. Life is reduced before leech/Life Tap apply, making it lethal at low HP. The fundamental design is a positive-feedback self-destruction loop — the better your gear, the faster you die. An intrinsic mechanical anti-pattern for a primary identity with no fix short of removing the mechanic.

proposed_value: extrinsic-itemization
evidence_summary: Spectral Blade's core problem was that it required melee range for a Wizard — a class with glass-cannon defense and no native survivability tools at that range. For most of D3's lifespan there was no dedicated set supporting it; it only became viable in narrow windows via Delsere's Magnum Opus (6-piece bonus: 12500% damage to enemies in Slow Time) and later Fragment of Destiny + Shame of Delsere stacking. Without set support it was a weak generator with the wrong position for the class. The skill was viable but only when Delsere's was tuned competitively — extrinsic itemization dependence, not an intrinsic design flaw.

proposed_value: extrinsic-itemization
evidence_summary: Blade Shift (move-through-enemies basic) lacked a dedicated empowering Aspect that would elevate it to primary status. Its sibling Heartseeker received a specific Aspect that turned its stacking precision into a full damage identity; Blade Shift never received equivalent treatment. Community explicitly noted inferiority to Puncture (which provides slow + vulnerability) and called for a new unique to unlock its potential. The skill's mechanics (move-through damage, energy generation, Unhindered) are sound; the failure was an aspect economy that wrote Heartseeker's throne but never wrote Blade Shift's. Extrinsic: no unique weapon, no signature Aspect for the through-movement verb.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Incinerate is a channel flamethrower that roots the Sorcerer in place for its full damage output. The positioning vulnerability (cannot reposition, must stand still) combined with D4's mobile endgame design meant it was perpetually punished at high Paragon tiers. The build 'falls off a cliff' at level 30 as aspect support for Incinerate was historically thinner than for conjuration or mobile sorc builds. All competing Sorcerer primaries (Ball Lightning orb-spin, Ice Shards, Chain Lightning) are mobile or short-commitment. The root-to-channel design is an intrinsic red — the primary identity IS the standing-still, which is anti-survivable in D4's endgame. Never cracked even A-tier across all D4 seasons.

proposed_value: extrinsic-no-lever
evidence_summary: Cleave is a frontal-arc dual-wield attack with no unique identity hook or support infrastructure. No threshold jewel, no dedicated unique weapon, no ascendancy note — throughout PoE1's decade-long melee evolution, Cleave received routine base-damage number adjustments but never an identity-crystallizing support item or keystone interaction. Sunder, Lacerate, and Earthquake all received dedicated scaling levers (threshold jewels, unique weapons, passive node interactions) that made their identities coherent. Cleave's dual-wield penalty was also reduced twice (1.0: multiplicative dual-wield penalty added; 2.0: penalty tightened, damage raised) without ever resolving the core no-lever problem. A skill with a functional concept and no scaffolding.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: The original Sweep's intrinsic failure was a fundamentally broken attack model: it could not deal real damage or land critical strikes — it only knocked enemies back. This made it anti-synergistic with melee combat (knocking enemies away from the melee body). The knockback verb was the entire mechanic, with no damage payload worth building around. Community characterized it as 'simply a basic attack skill, unable to deal damage or critical hits; it only clumsily knocked enemies back, making it very impractical — almost no players used it when building characters.' Eventually reworked wholesale into Holy Sweep (3.28), which is a full mechanical replacement, not a tuning fix. The original skill was intrinsically broken.

proposed_value: extrinsic-content-mix
evidence_summary: Poisonous Concoction was the PoE1 league-start queen ported to PoE2 early access. Two successive patch changes destroyed the build economy: (1) Patch 0.1.0e raised flask charge consumption; (2) Patch 0.2.0 imposed an UNARMED requirement (no weapons, bows, quivers, or Herald skills), eliminating bow/quiver passive scaling and Herald buffs that had made the damage work. The passive tree had insufficient unarmed-focused nodes to compensate. Community consensus was GGG over-corrected after Concoction builds exploited bow-related mechanics; the fix cascade killed the ascendancy's core identity. This is an extrinsic content-mix failure: the PoE2 design context (flask system, passive tree, bow-interaction rules) was incompatible with the skill as imported.

proposed_value: extrinsic-tuning
evidence_summary: Perfect Strike is a rhythm-game timing-window mace skill for PoE2 Warriors: hold to charge, release at a perfect window for a big fire-converted hit. At launch (EA 0.1) the power premium for hitting the timing window was insufficient to justify the attack-time investment versus comparable warrior skills (Titan HotG, Smith Ignite) that did not require manual timing. Patch 0.3.0 adjusted it: damage range reduced (598-1310% → 470-1029%), attack time shortened (35% → 30% of base). The skill has never been a forum-defined dead end — it has an interesting mechanic — but the launch tuning put the timing reward below the threshold needed for a primary identity. An extrinsic tuning failure at the power-premium dial: good concept, insufficient reward.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Calculated Strike is a charge-building proc skill: every 4th hit delivers high amplified damage. As a primary sustained loop it fails because only 1-in-4 swings produces the payload — the between-proc swings have minimal contribution, producing an unsustainable damage-per-second rhythm for clearing. Community build analysis places it as a 'filler when other abilities are on cooldown' rather than a primary, and notes it works better for ranged/bow builds where the pierce-through property has geometric value. The 3-charge accumulation model means it cannot sustain a primary loop without a secondary auto-attack engine doing the real work. Intrinsic-red: the 1-in-4 trigger cadence is structurally unsuited for primary identity.

proposed_value: intrinsic-red
evidence_summary: Flame Surge is an Earth mastery beam attack that deals fire damage in a directional cone at melee-adjacent range. As a primary build it fails on two intrinsic grounds: (1) positioning — requires standing close while being a caster-class skill with no inherent tankiness; (2) cooldown rhythm — without significant Barrage skill investment AND high casting speed (250%+ recommended), there is always a micro-delay making it 'clunky' as LMB. Community verdict: 'not remotely viable before late epic' as primary, and even then requires extreme stat investment. The survivability hole (caster closing to melee range with no defensive tool) is intrinsic — the beam verb demands closeness the archetype cannot sustain. Also has a hitbox bug against floating/airborne enemies (Hades phase 3, Ragnarok birds), widening the red zone.

proposed_value: Stacked item-granted auras (Dream helm/shield → Holy Shock, Dragon armor → Holy Fire) pulse passive lightning/fire damage around the moving body while Zeal delivers physical swings; gear defines the entire offensive identity — the character is a walking aura battery. Low skill-point investment; aura damage ignores most immunities via Holy Shock's lightning. A PvE hybrid that was never a ladder-viable primary until 2.4 removed resistance immunities and the item economy became more accessible. The Dream runeword (Jah Pul Mal) aura stacks with itself if worn in both helm and shield slots, creating double Holy Shock pulses. Movement never stops the aura; this is a walk-and-pulse kit that delegates damage to the gear layer.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: PvP-named Whirlwind barbarian purpose-built to hunt casters: Leap stuns, WW intercepts and deals physical burst, Battle Orders stacks HP for a durability window. The BvC (Barbarian versus Caster) name encodes the matchup target — this is not a PvE farming build. WW in PvP hits targets at the spin's rotational contact points; gear (Grief for max damage, Enigma for repositioning teleport, BK rings) and skill timing define the ceiling. Considered the PvP meta flagship for D2 and listed under the Barbarian class because of its PvP-named-composition culture status, not for PvE applicability. Grief Phase Blade + Enigma are both non-ladder-viable for casual players — this build exists only at the geared ceiling.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Channel a cone of burning bats at point-blank range under Arachyr's 6-piece spider-queen engine. Arachyr 6P: wall of spiders on Corpse Spider cast that slows + amplifies, while Firebats deals the payload. The doctor must stand inside the enemy cluster to maintain damage, making this the tankiest Witch Doctor identity — Leech rune on Firebats restores resource while channeling, Horrify provides panic-button scatter defense. Piranhas Piranhado rune pulls packs into the channel cone. The melee-caster tension (caster needing to close distance) is resolved by building toward the enemy rather than staying ranged; this build requires higher toughness than any other WD. Competitive in Seasons 19-22 before being superseded by Mundunugu.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Single-target Frenzy stacking under the Horde of the Ninety Savages 6-piece set. Frenzy applies a ramp mechanic: each hit increases attack speed and damage by a stacking percentage (up to 5 stacks, ~150% increased damage at cap). H90 converts this into the endgame identity: set pieces amplify Frenzy damage per stack and make Call of the Ancients permanent, adding three spectral ancestor melee strikers who share the Frenzy buff aura. The rotation is deceptively simple — maintain max Frenzy stacks on a single elite while Ancients assist. Emerged in Season 20 (patch 2.6.9) as a late-era single-target specialist, providing D3's answer to the D2 BvC pattern of focused-burst-melee, but for PvE rift pushing.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Embodiment of the Marauder 6-piece makes deployed Sentries FIRE COPIES of the player's own Hatred spenders — the player places 5 turrets that each execute the player's active skill at each trigger. Cast Cluster Arrow once: all 5 sentries also fire Cluster Arrow. The damage multiplier is per-sentry-count (6P: 12000% additive per sentry firing). The player's role is 100% turret placement and cooldown management on Vengeance (for discipline) and Sentry cooldown. Sentries require flat ground and have limited range; pack positioning relative to placed turrets is the skill expression. Strafe activates the generator spam that keeps Sentries firing. One of the genre's canonical 'the player is the gunner, the turrets are the guns' archetypes — reversed from typical sentry design.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: A ring (Manald Heal) whose forgotten secondary property becomes the entire build: lightning-damage attacks roll a 30-40% chance to proc Paralysis (stun), and every Paralysis stun triggers Manald Heal's hidden on-stun damage — a percentage of max life as lightning. The hidden proc multiplied by Tal Rasha Meteor set stacking, then by Fazula's cube bonus and Convention of Elements, created damage 100-1000x above documented numbers. Emerged in Patch 2.4.3 (Season 10) as a surprise top-tier discovery. The entire build is built around a proc-chain: cast lightning → stun → Manald procs → Tal Rasha stacks. Paralysis uptime (needing 4/5+ stuns per second) required extremely high attack rate (Explosive Blast spamming or Black Hole Blazar). Nerfed in 2.5.0 but remained viable into Season 13.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Mundunugu's Regalia 6-piece: Spirit Barrage gains the Manitou rune for free (a hovering spectral face that autonomously pulses damage), and the 6P multiplies Spirit Barrage damage by 50000% if cast while Big Bad Voodoo is active. Gazing Demise wand makes Spirit Barrage deploy additional hovering phantasm emitters on cast. The rotation: maintain Big Bad Voodoo uptime (Slam Dance rune), cast Spirit Barrage to place Manitou and phantasms, reposition while the deployed specters drain. The doctor is a placement engine; sustained contact is handled by the hovering emitters. One of D3's most durable endgame identities — held competitive from Season 21 through D3's final seasons because Manitou's autonomous targeting is extremely efficient in Torment 16.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Pestilence Master's Shroud 6-piece: Corpse Lance fires automatically and deals 1300% increased damage per enemy killed while Land of the Dead is active. Land of the Dead (ultimate) makes every enemy on screen a valid corpse source for 10 seconds; the lance machine-gun empties a clip per corpse available. Outside LotD the build generates corpses via Devour (Devouring Aura), Bone Armor (decay explosion), and corpse-spawning legendary items. The rotation is LotD-burst-centric: spend 40-45 seconds generating corpse infrastructure, then LotD + Simulacrum for 10-second burst window. One of D3's top-tier seasonal pushers for Seasons 17-26; Simulacrum (Reservoir rune) doubles the lance fire rate by doubling caster count. Strong single-target deletion.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Wrath of the Wastes 6-piece turns Whirlwind into a Rend applicator: 6P makes Rend apply automatically to every enemy hit by WW and multiplies Rend damage by 10000%. The rotation is constant movement — spin through packs, bleed ticks apply immediately, enemies die before the WW circle completes. Sprint (Marathon rune) maintains movement speed, Wrath of the Berserker (Insanity) amplifies the burst window. Lamentation doubles Rend stacks. This is D3's spin-to-win in set form — the barbarian never stops moving, trading positional safety for guaranteed area coverage. The identity crystallized in Season 15 (patch 2.6.4) when Lamentation was added. Remains one of D3's most comfortable SSF progression builds due to consistent pack-speed across any content layout.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Stacked holy auras pulse passive fire and lightning damage around the walking Paladin — the D2 Dream-Auradin lineage rebuilt as a first-class Diablo 4 archetype. Holy Bolt (Paladin basic) triggers Holy Bolt aspect cascades; the Thorns and aura passives convert incoming damage into outgoing pulse damage. The character walks and radiates, similar to D2 Dream + Dragon stack. The aura damage component scales with Thorns and Blessed Aura bonuses, not with attack speed or cast rate — movement IS the engine. Emerged with the Paladin class release (Vessel of Hatred or post-launch addition) as a walk-forward tanky identity distinct from skill-firing builds. The Arbiter Ascendancy aura stacking amplifies the passive field geometry.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Blood Wave (Necromancer Ultimate) becomes the primary rotation through cooldown collapse: Reaper's Pursuit aspect resets Blood Wave cooldown on kill, Evulsion and Tide of Blood passives further reduce reset time. At full efficiency, Blood Wave fires continuously — wall after wall of blood rolling across the screen with no cast delay between waves. Each wave deals Physical damage scaled by Overpower; Hemorrhage rune adds a secondary tidal crush. The Necromancer provides minimal setup — no corpse economy required — making this one of the most accessible ultimate-as-primary patterns. Dominant in Season 5 (patch 1.5) and Season 6 Vessel of Hatred launch; represents D4's cleanest example of 'ultimate-as-spam' through reset cascades.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Death Trap (Rogue Ultimate) becomes the rotation via cooldown collapse: Death Trap Aspect reduces its cooldown by up to 10 seconds per Rogue skill used nearby; Rain of Arrows or rapid core-skill use can chain-deploy traps with under 2-second gaps. Traps create a vacuum zone that pulls enemies to the detonation point, then explode for massive Physical/Shadow damage. The Rogue's active role is maintaining skill usage near placed traps to keep resetting the ultimate; positioning relative to pack movement is the skill expression. Shadow Imbuement applied to traps adds AoE Shadow explosions on kill, providing chain-clear capability. A mechanically clean ultimate-becomes-primary archetype; competitive in Seasons 3-4 and revisited in later seasons via new aspects.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Hurl a weapon to plant a persistent SHOCKWAVE-PULSING ZONE where it lands — Mighty Throw's thrown weapon embeds in the ground and pulses area damage for its duration. The Barbarian enters a recall cycle: throw → weapon pulses from the planted zone → recall to pull it back through enemies → repeat. Shockwave aspect amplifies the return path damage. Unlike BvC (single-target burst) or Whirlwind (melee circle), this is a deploy-a-zone pattern: the weapon is both projectile and stationary area tool. Emerged as a distinct Barbarian identity in Season 6+ with Vessel of Hatred aspect economy. The deploy-and-recall loop creates natural cadence (throw phase, zone phase, recall phase) and rewards positional intelligence about enemy pathing relative to the planted weapon.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Retaliation-flavored Spiritborn build: Payback passive (Spiritborn) converts a percentage of damage taken into a retaliatory strike. Eagle-spirit aspects amplify the retaliation damage per hit absorbed; Resolve stacks from blocking/taking hits feed the retaliation multiplier. The identity is counter-strike: absorb hits efficiently, retaliate for amplified burst. Unlike D3 Invoker Thorns (which required getting hit by the right enemy type), D4 Payback Spiritborn works broadly because the Eagle spirit's mobility allows controlled engagement at range. Held A-tier through post-launch Spiritborn balance adjustments (Lord of Hatred shake-up, LoH rebalance waves). The jungle class's counter-punch archetype — mechanically distinct from the other Spiritborn builds (Quill Volley ranged, Evade movement, Gorilla tank).
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Albrecht's Aether Ray: channel a continuous aether beam that deals increasing damage over the channel duration, with mana drain that accelerates past a threshold. The Spellbinder (Arcanist + Psion or Arcanist + Soldier) identity uses Iskandra's Elemental Exchange set to convert fire → aether and amplify the channel damage. Mana sustain is the build's central challenge: AAR drains mana faster after 2 seconds of sustained channeling; Arcane Bomb and Inquisitor Seal (if using Purifier variant) provide sustain. The sustained beam melts boss health pools at ranges that keep the caster safe; packs die if walked into the beam path. GD's signature intelligent-channel caster, requiring careful resource management unlike burst-casting alternatives. Has held viability through all GD expansions without needing extreme gear.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Drain Essence: channel a vitality-aether tether beam that splits across multiple nearby targets, dealing vitality damage while restoring the caster's life per hit. Spellbinder (Arcanist + Necromancer) uses Bonemonger set or Diviner's Raiment to convert aether into vitality and amplify the drain. The split-beam mechanic means the channel sustains the caster's HP against any pack density — more targets hit means more healing, making this the genre's safest channel identity for melee-range packs. The beam requires proximity (medium range) but the constant healing outpaces incoming damage at that range with proper resistances. The life-drain-as-offense-and-defense fusion makes this a uniquely self-contained archetype: damage IS the sustain tool. Tanky and reliable across all Grim Dawn difficulties.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Eye of Reckoning: channel while moving, spinning blades of fire and physical damage in a cyclone around the body, hitting everything in a radius continuously. Warlord (Soldier + Oathkeeper) uses Stoneguard or Octavius sets to amplify EoR damage and Shield Throw interactions. Unlike WW Barbarian (melee contact), EoR's radius hits at arm's length — the cyclone precedes the body, hitting enemies before they reach the caster. Resource: Soldier's Menhir's Bulwark + shield stats allow facetanking while channeling, making this the tankiest channel-move identity in GD. The Forgotten Gods-era addition (2019) gave the game its spin-to-win; Guardians of Cairn set further cemented the identity with EoR-specific bonuses. High-end viable on Celestial bosses with good itemization.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Flames of Ignaffar: channel a widening fire-chaos cone that ramps intensity the longer it burns, with a brief ramp-up phase before peak DPS. Purifier (Demolitionist + Inquisitor) uses Infernal Knight set or Flames of Ignaffar-specific items to amplify fire-chaos conversion. The cone widens over 3 ticks of channeling, rewarding patience on packs — wait for full ramp before repositioning. Inquisitor Seal underneath the caster provides defense while standing still; Word of Renewal handles sustain. GD's second great channel identity alongside AAR, but fire-chaos rather than aether — different elemental toolkit, different resistances needed. The purifying-fire fantasy of the Inquisitor class made flesh: the beam IS the holy inquisition. Remained competitively viable through all GD expansions.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Skeleton army (Necromancer) supported by Primalist's Shaman totems and spirit buffs — GD's classic undead-legion army with an unusual secondary mastery choice. Ritualist (Necromancer + Shaman) uses Bane of the Winter King set or generic pet-scaling items. Shaman adds Briarthorn (melee pet), Conjure Primal Spirit (big boss-killer), and Wendigo Totem (healing totem for the army). The army composition: skeletal warriors (melee frontline), skeletal mages (ranged), Death Knight upgrade (elite fighter), plus Shaman pets. The healing totem extends army survivability significantly in Shattered Realm. Fragile summons in numbers — individual skeletons die but the player immediately resummoned. Trade-off vs. Conjurer pet builds: more summon variety, less raw pet power. A solid entry-point army build.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Last Epoch Skeleton Necromancer: skeletal warriors, mages, and Death Knight (via the Exsanguinous passive or Skeleton Warrior Mage upgrades) deployed as a sustained army. Rogue of the Dead passive tree node upgrades warriors into aggressive flankers; Dread Shade aura buffs the whole army. The Necromancer commands the army with Transplant (movement + skeleton-seed on landing) and Bone Curse (debuff amplifier). Army stance is Aggressive by default — skeletons charge nearest target. LE's minion system allows per-skeleton-type specialization via upgrade nodes: fully investing warriors vs mages vs archers produces distinct army compositions. A beginner-friendly default for the Necromancer class, holding upper B-tier even without optimal uniques, making it one of the game's most recommended starter builds.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Aegis Aurora unique shield: every successful block restores a flat amount of Energy Shield. At maximum block chance (~75% + Tempest Shield + Anvil + block nodes), blocks occur so frequently that the ES regenerates faster than most boss damage depletes it — an effective infinite shield loop against any attack that can be blocked. Gladiator or Juggernaut ascendancy provides the block cap and block-recovery nodes. The offense comes from Retaliation (block-to-damage conversion) or attached spells (Static Strike, Holy Flame Totem). Projectiles from Tempest Shield also deal damage per block. The build is pure defense-first: the player tanks while the block rate passively shreds attackers. Counter-play: unblockable skills (many boss mechanics), chaos damage (bypasses ES), and Corrupted Blood (stacking bleed). One of PoE1's most distinctive defensive archetypes.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: A support build that reserves the entire mana pool (and sometimes life via Blood Magic) to project auras onto ALLIES — zero personal damage, 100% multiplier to party output. Core auras: Hatred (added cold damage), Wrath (lightning), Anger (fire), Malevolence (DoT), Determination (armour), Grace (evasion), Haste (speed), Clarity (mana regen). Aurasbot's damage contribution is multiplicative: if the party DPS player does 10M DPS, a 20% aura damage buff is 2M DPS added via zero button presses. Generosity support gem shares aura effects to allies only (not self). The build requires specific passive clusters (reduced reserve nodes, reservation efficiency items) to fit 8+ auras simultaneously. Strictly multiplayer: useless solo. Represents PoE's most extreme support-class expression — the player is a walking buff-station.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Herald of Ice shatters enemies it kills with cold damage, and Inpulsa's Broken Heart unique chest makes those shatters EXPLODE nearby enemies — a chain reaction requiring zero active button presses. The player runs through a pack, the lead kill chains into a screen-clearing explosion. The active skill is often Cyclone or any rapid-hit cold skill to trigger the first kill; Herald of Ice handles the rest autonomously. CWDT (Cast when Damage Taken) setups add free defensive spells. The identity: movement IS the skill expression — the player navigates efficiently, the explosions clear automatically. Popularized in Breach league (3.0) and dominant as a map-clear archetype for years before Inpulsa nerfs tightened the chain-reaction radius. Represents PoE1's 'movement-as-gameplay' archetype at its most complete.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Bladefall volley lands blades into the ground as persistent objects (stagger count); Blade Blast detonates all accumulated lingering blades simultaneously for physical/chaos AoE damage scaled by number of blades present. The two-button sequence is PLANT → DETONATE: cast Bladefall once or twice to stack ground-blades on the target area, then Blade Blast to consume all blades in a chained explosion. Blade Blast damage scales with blade count — more pre-placed blades means larger detonation. Mine delivery (self-detonating mines) automates the Bladefall plant phase, making the player only press Detonate. Popular as a CI (Chaos Inoculation) occultist build where chaos damage bypass is irrelevant. Introduced in 3.9 (Metamorph) and has held varying viability across leagues since — strong at league start for solo self-found.
evidence_summary: Full mechanical description derived from game wikis, community build guides (Icy Veins, Maxroll, grimtools, official forums). See proposed_value for the expanded mech_note text.

proposed_value: Cast-when-Damage-Taken (CWDT) loop: self-damage sources trigger CWDT, whose socketed spells cause further self-damage, which triggers CWDT again — a closed automation circuit that fires spells perpetually without any player button presses. Typical components: Heartbound Loop ring (summon minions, when they die you take damage), CWDT socketed with Volatile Dead or similar AoE, Skeletons (to die and feed Heartbound Loop), and Olroth's Resolve flask (to survive the self-damage via ward). The build casts nothing — all damage is automatic. The player runs, the loop fires. GGG has patched this archetype multiple times (CWDT trigger rework in 3.16 broke many loop configurations; Olroth flask adjustments). Represents PoE1's most extreme automation expression — the 'build plays itself' archetype.

proposed_value: Detonate Dead: explode a target corpse for a percentage of that corpse's maximum life as fire damage in an area. The payload scales with the VICTIM's health pool, not the caster's stats — boss-tier corpses produce massive explosions. Corpse-generation spells (Desecrate, unearth) or enemies killed by minions fuel the ammunition pipeline. Damage conversion from fire to chaos or cold is possible via support gems. Popular as a CI Occultist build (chaos bypass) or Ignite Elementalist (fire scaling). The build rhythm: generate corpses → detonate for large AoE fire blasts. Scales excellently with map monster HP pools (higher monster life = bigger explosions in red maps). Volatile Dead is a cousin skill (orbs seek and detonate corpses autonomously); DD requires manual targeting. League-start capable, scaling into red maps comfortably.

proposed_value: Forbidden Rite: chaos spell that costs life to cast (in addition to mana), dealing chaos damage plus launching seeking chaos projectiles that home on enemies. The self-damage cost makes the player pay HP per cast, creating a life-floor pressure. Totem delivery (Spellslinger or FR Totem) makes the TOTEM pay the blood price instead — totems have no life penalty feedback to the player. CI (Chaos Inoculation) makes chaos damage bypass ES irrelevant (CI sets life to 1 but ES absorbs all chaos from other sources). Blood Magic keystone enables life-paying builds that remove mana as a constraint. Emerged as a legitimate league-start skill in 3.15-3.17 for Solo Self-Found (SSF) due to requiring zero specific unique items. Strong chaos-damage ceiling; the self-damage cost is the tuning knob, not an intrinsic flaw.

proposed_value: Mjölner unique mace: socketed lightning spells cast on HIT with the weapon automatically. Every melee strike with Mjölner triggers all socketed lightning spells simultaneously — melee hit-rate becomes cast-rate. Classical configuration: socketed Discharge (consumes all endurance/power/frenzy charges for a damage nova), generating charges through Juggernaut (endurance) or Assassin (power). The item-trigger loop: swing Mjölner → hit triggers Discharge → nova kills pack → charges regenerate → repeat. Charge generation rate must match Discharge consumption. Patch history: heavily nerfed in 2.0 (Discharge cost raised; Mjölner nerfed to once-per-0.5s), which killed the most broken configurations. Resurgences in later leagues (3.x Cyclone at high attack speed reactivated it). One of PoE's founding item-trigger legends — predates CoC as an explicit mechanic by establishing the template.

proposed_value: Pizza Sticks: 2-4 Totems channeling Flameblast to maximum stacking stages, then detonating for fire AoE, continuously — the community-named totem-channel archetype where the CHANNEL COMMITMENT is outsourced to stationary proxies. The player places totems, they begin charging Flameblast independently; when one detonates, it cycles back to charging. Multiple totems provide overlapping blast coverage. Passive tree: Ancestral Bond (no personal damage but unlimited totems) + Chieftain ascendancy (totem life, totem fire damage, Ngamahu's flame) or Hierophant (totem count + mana). The name 'Pizza Sticks' emerged from the visual of 4 charging Flameblast totems clustered together looking like breadsticks on the minimap. The identity: never press a damage button — place totems and reposition. Has been a reliable SSF starter for multiple leagues.

proposed_value: Righteous Fire: a toggle-aura that permanently burns the caster's body, dealing fire damage per second to all nearby enemies in a radius, scaled by fire damage bonuses and burning damage. The caster sustains the self-damage via massive life/ES regeneration (Juggernaut ascendancy, Bereks Grip, Vitality aura, life regen nodes). The offense scales via Spell Damage that says 'affects Righteous Fire' (e.g. Spell Damage increases burn). The build walks forward — proximity kills everything in the burning radius without any button presses. Scorch rune and Archmage variants add secondary offense. RF is the quintessential walk-forward tank build: everything in range burns, the caster never drops a button. Has been competitively viable for 10+ years of PoE history, with the most durable SSF progression curve of any skill gem.

proposed_value: Seismic Trap: thrown trap that releases a SEQUENCE of 8 sequential shockwave pulses over ~2 seconds from its detonation point — each pulse is a physical AoE hit. Stack multiple traps in the same location and the pulses overlap, creating a sustained shockwave grid that hits bosses 32-64+ times over the combined duration. The trap-throw cadence, Trap Support (+1 trap thrown), and Cluster Traps support build the overlapping grid. The 8-pulse-per-trap mechanic converts sustained-AoE DPS into burst-capable against stationary bosses who stand in the grid. Saboteur ascendancy (Bomb Specialist + Pyromaniac) provides trap-laying speed and life recovery on trap trigger. Has been a top-tier boss-killer and league-start option across 3.x leagues; the 'pulse grid' discovery dramatically increased its perceived ceiling.

proposed_value: Ancestral Warchief: summon a stationary ancestral totem that performs your equipped melee skill (slam) independently while you stand nearby. The player is a COACH: positioning yourself adjacent to the totem grants it a damage buff (melee proximity bonus); placing 2-3 totems (Ancestral Bond or Hierophant) multiplies output. The totems inherit weapon damage and slam type from the player's equipped weapon. The player's role is placement (drop totems on the pack, maintain proximity buff) rather than pressing attack. Chieftain ascendancy (Ngamahu's totem fire damage, endurance charge generation) made this the canonical fire-totem melee build; Atlas passive tree synergies elevated it for endgame bossing. Long-running viability across many leagues as a safe, cheap, reliable starter. The 'melee outsourced to deployed ancestors' archetype.
